title: Promotion arbitration flap causing traffic saturation and pinned-version drift
creator: Maya Chen
description: During a scheduled canary promotion for a language model variant, concurrent promotion logic from two controllers produced conflicting route updates. The arbitration flap briefly sent >3x intended traffic to canary endpoints, saturating dedicated pools and leaving the older pinned version in a stuck state. Several customer requests experienced 503s and elevated latency for ~23 minutes. Rollback attempts were blocked by a pin-state race, complicating mitigation.
timeline: 2026-03-10T09:02:14Z - Start: staged canary promotion triggered by rollout pipeline (auto-promote enabled, controlled by rollout-controller-v2).
2026-03-10T09:03:01Z - Race: legacy pin-manager service received a parallel manual pin reconcile request from an operator and attempted to re-assert the previous pin state.

2026-03-10T09:03:04Z - Flap observed: route-translator processed conflicting deltas; both 'promote-weights' and 'pin-lock' deltas applied within same transaction window, producing overlapping routing rules for the canary shard.

2026-03-10T09:03:20Z - Surge: canary endpoint traffic spikes to ~320% of expected load, triggering GPU queueing and token-level stalls. Errors begin surfacing in frontend metrics (503s and grpc deadlines).
2026-03-10T09:05:00Z - Detection: SRE alert (rollouts.error_rate > 1.5% for 3m) fires; on-call triage begins.
2026-03-10T09:07:30Z - Mitigation attempt: operator issues immediate rollback via the console; rollout-controller rejects rollback because pin-manager reports an active pin lease (pin lock race).
2026-03-10T09:15:40Z - Manual intervention: SRE applies emergency rate-limit on canary route via feature gate (circuit-breaker to 10% traffic) to stabilize user traffic.
2026-03-10T09:25:00Z - Recovery: traffic stabilizes; queued requests drained; error rates return to baseline by 09:35Z.
2026-03-10T09:35:10Z - Postmortem: root cause triage begins; decision made to create follow-up tickets for lock/coordination fixes and rollout hardening.
impact_summary: Approx 23 minutes of elevated errors and latency for affected customers in region eu-west-1. About 0.4% of provisioned requests experienced 503 or deadline exceeded; a small set of enterprise customers using pinned versions saw temporary request failures when the pinned version became unreachable due to capacity stress. No data leakage or model corruption detected.
root_cause: Two independent components (rollout-controller-v2 and legacy pin-manager) attempted to update route state concurrently without cross-service coordination or lease-based arbitration. The route-translator accepted both deltas in quick succession because there was no global ordering guarantee for 'pin' vs 'promote' operations. This produced conflicting rule fragments that temporarily duplicated traffic paths to the canary pool, exceeding capacity and preventing clean rollback due to a stale pin lease.
detection: Automatic alerting on rollouts.error_rate and token-queue-latency triggered detection. A subsequent Grafana graph for 'route-state-change-frequency' highlighted an unusually high rate of state flips in the 2m window.
mitigation: Applied emergency traffic cap to canary route via console feature gate (circuit-breaker at 10%) to protect general capacity.
Manually revoked the stale pin lease from pin-manager to allow rollback path to complete.
Scaled up canary pool capacity by +2 nodes in eu-west-1 to speed draining of queued requests.
Notified impacted customers and followed up with incident summary emails.
long_term_action_items: Add optimistic-leasing to pin-manager: route-state transitions must acquire a short-lived global lease before applying pin or promote deltas (owner: Priya Patel, ETA: 2026-04-05).
Introduce a 'transition coordinator' that serializes promote/pin/op overrides for the same logical route to prevent interleaved writes (owner: Noah Martinez, ETA: 2026-04-10).
Implement pre-apply sanity checks in route-translator to reject deltas that would produce overlapping prefixes or duplicate paths into the same backend pool (owner: Liam O'Rourke, ETA: 2026-04-01).
Add a canary promotion circuit-breaker at the routing layer to enforce a maximum burst factor (default 1.5x) and configurable per-tenant caps (owner: infra-sre, ETA: 2026-04-15).
Improve rollback logic to bypass stale pin leases by verifying control-plane consensus (owner: Maya Chen, ETA: 2026-03-25).
Add deterministic e2e test that simulates concurrent pin+promote requests and validates that route state remains consistent under race conditions (owner: QA Team, ETA: 2026-03-29).
Dashboard: expose 'route-transition-latency' and 'pin-lease-age' on rollout console to detect early arbitration flaps (owner: Observability team, ETA: 2026-03-30).
review_notes: PM review (Elena Ruiz): prioritize safe-fast mitigations first (circuit-breaker + rollback bypass) before coordination refactor.
Design review (Arjun Singh): recommended UX guardrails in Console to make 'force pin' an explicit destructive action with 2-step confirmation and admin-only role.
Security review (Samantha Lowe): no secrets exposed; however recommended audit logs be extended for route delta origin to improve post-incident traceability.
SRE feedback: add synthetic canary traffic tests during promotions to detect capacity saturation pre-apply.
followup_meeting: 2026-03-18T10:00:00Z - Postmortem review with Eng, SRE, PM, Design
verification_criteria: No route-state flip > 3s for same logical route under concurrent change simulation in CI (target: pass for 1000 runs).
Regression test showing rollback can complete if pin-lease age > 30s without manual intervention.
Observed 95th percentile route-transition-latency <= 150ms in runtime-1.22 after fixes for 7 days in staging and canary regions.
final_status: Pending signoff from Eng leadership and PM. Action owners assigned; several critical fixes targeted for runtime-1.22 minor patch releases.
